note: side effect: collapses every '//' in the whole URL, so a path or query that contains '//' (e.g. '?next=//x') is changed too
issue: join_url() doubles the slash when the base ends with '/' or the path starts with one: join_url('https://api.test/', '/v1/items') gives 'https://api.test///v1/items'.
